info.name: Tayara - Support chat (real-time Kafka/SSE, presence, attachments)
info.description:
End-to-end collection for the support chat module (`/api/v1/support`).

Covers: ticket + conversation bootstrap (welcome message), message append with dense `seq` and `client_msg_id` idempotency, hash chain, message history/replay, attachment upload + one-time link + gated download, presence/last-seen batch read, authorization negatives, and the staff inbox / assignment / quality review / runtime settings surface.

**Run order matters.** Run folders top to bottom (Collection Runner). `Auth` stores tokens, `1. Ticket & conversation` stores `ticketId` / `conversationId`, and later folders reuse them.

Prerequisites:
- API running on `{{baseUrl}}` against the seeded demo DB (`ahmed.ali` / `fatima.z` / `admin@tayara.test`, password `123456`).
- `X-token` = customer JWT, `S-token` = staff JWT (the collection sends `x-token` for both, which the guard groups accept).
- Attachments use the existing `utils/upload` local OSS (`oss-type: local`), so files land in `local.store-path` and are served only through `GET /attachments/:uuid`.

**SSE:** Postman renders a streamed response, but its test scripts only run when the request finishes, so the stream request stays open on purpose. For an interactive browser session open `{{baseUrl}}/api/v1/support/sse-client` (served by the API), or run the live checks:
`SUPPORT_REDIS_ADDR=localhost:6379 go test ./service/support/... -run LiveRedis -v` and `KAFKA_BROKERS=localhost:9092 go test ./service/support/... -run LiveKafka -v`.

item.name: 2. Messages (append, ordering, idempotency)
item.description: Every message persists first, gets a dense `seq` under a lock, links into a SHA-256 hash chain, and publishes to Kafka when the bus is enabled. `clientMsgId` makes retries safe.

request.description: A fresh `clientMsgId` is generated in the pre-request script. Stores `messageUuid` and `seq`.

exec: pm.test('seq follows the welcome message', () => pm.expect(json.data.seq).to.be.above(1));

request.description: The unique `(conversation_id, client_msg_id)` index plus a pre-check returns the original row, never a duplicate.
Ordered by `seq`. Clients replay from `sinceSeq` after reconnecting the SSE stream.

3. Attachments
item.description: Attachments go through the existing `utils/upload` OSS layer (`UploadFileWithPath(file, "support-chat")`). Validation (size, extension, sniffed MIME) happens **before** a byte is written; a message claims an attachment exactly once (`uploaded -> attached`).

request.description: Pick a real `.png`/`.jpg`/`.webp`/`.gif`/`.pdf` file for the `file` field (or set the `attachmentFile` variable to its path). Allowed MIME defaults: jpeg/png/webp/gif/pdf, max 10 MiB.
Body may be empty when at least one attachment is claimed. The claim and the message insert commit in one transaction.

item.name: Reuse an already-linked attachment is rejected

exec: pm.test('422: attachment is no longer uploaded', () => pm.response.to.have.status(422));

request.description: Authorization is by UUID + `CanRead`, never by a caller-supplied path. Local OSS serves the file; remote backends 302 to the stored URL.

request.description: Set the `badAttachmentFile` variable to a real file named `.zip`/`.txt`/`.exe` (or select one for the `file` field). `utils/upload`'s extension allowlist and the runtime MIME allowlist both reject it, so the upload must fail with 422 **before** anything is written to disk.

exec: pm.test('422 for a disallowed extension', () => pm.response.to.have.status(422));

item.name: 4. Real-time (SSE + presence + last seen)
item.description: The stream is fed by the per-instance Kafka fanout (or the local hub when `support.kafka.enabled=false`). Frames: `message.created`, `presence.changed`, `closing`; a `: ping` comment every 15s. Presence is Redis-only and refcounted; transitions publish once per 0->1 / 1->0.

request.description: Postman shows the live stream in the response pane.
